BackStep.description:
The `back` payload (`- back: {}`).

It has no target: Back goes to the focused window. SE1's opt-in `expect_change` is the only field, so `- back: {}` keeps parsing.

expect_change.description: SE1: fail the step when the settled frame's pixels are unchanged.

Bounds.description:
Integer screen bounds `[left, top, right, bottom]` in pixels.

Serialized as a four-element array. `right`/`bottom` are exclusive at the Android/UI-automator pixel-grid level.

activity.description: Activity component (defaults to the launched activity).

name.description: Artifact name (`frames/<seq>.png` is always written; this names the step).

DisplaySpec.description:
The display a session renders to.

`none` is headless: capture/observe must return `NO_DISPLAY` instead of silently allocating a surface.

oneOf.description: No display at all (headless logic/storage tests).
Offscreen software surface with an explicit size and density.

density_dpi.description: Density in dots per inch (for example 420).

Engine.description: Which engine should run the scenario.

oneOf.description: Use the native runtime when it can, otherwise fall back per policy.
Only the native runtime; never fall back.

Expectation.description: What the scenario expects. Used to make negative tests explicit.

oneOf.description: The scenario must produce `status: fail` (the app ran; a check did not hold).
The scenario must produce any non-pass status (crash/unsupported/... count).

code.description: Error code the run must report (`ASSERTION_FAILED`, `TIMEOUT`, ...).

reason.description: Optional `details.reason` the failing step's error must carry (for example `content_settle_pixel` or `content-not-stable`).

FallbackPolicy.description: What to do when the preferred engine cannot run a step.

oneOf.description: Report the native result and escalate to the reference backend when allowed.
Report the native result only; never silently switch engines.
Forbid fallback; an unsupported capability stays unsupported.

IsolationLevel.description:
How independent a session is from other sessions.

The levels are ordered from cheapest/weakest to strongest. A claim of data independence is only allowed at `sandbox` and above, and only when the engine actually implements the guarantees (see `docs/AGENT_API.md`).

oneOf.description: Another activity/task in a shared process and shared app data. No isolation.
Separate process, potentially the same package/storage identity.
Separate process/UID/credentials/mount namespace and app data.
Fully separate engine instance (strongest short of a VM).
Sandboxed full Android/backend for untrusted or device-level fidelity.

expect_change.description: SE1: fail the step when the settled frame's pixels are unchanged.

settle.description: Settle rule for this input (`strict` default, `fast` navigation).

settle_timeout_ms.description: P12b: strict/fast settle deadline for this key action (milliseconds).

settle.description: SE2: settle rule for the launch's first tree (`strict` default, `content` for a screen whose tree is stable while its pixels animate). A launch's frame is never pixel evidence under `content`, so a later pixel assertion bound to it fails closed.

settle_timeout_ms.description: P12b: strict/fast settle deadline for the first tree (milliseconds).

LogAssertion.description:
Assert a logcat-style line sequence.

Each pattern is a Rust regex. With `ordered: true` the patterns must match in order (extra lines are allowed); with `ordered: false` each pattern must match at least once.

min_matches.description: Minimum number of matched lines required per pattern.

patterns.description: Regex patterns to match against log messages.

since_previous_step.description: Only consider log events produced since the previous scenario step. This is what makes lifecycle assertions step-scoped instead of matching an earlier cycle.

tag.description: Log tag to filter on (for example `AcosFixture`).

times.description: Match at most this many times (absent = unlimited).

NoCrashAssertion.description: Assert that no crash/ANR event occurred.

RegionAssertion.description:
A host-side pixel/region assertion over one freshly captured frame.

**Coordinates are display pixels** (the same space as UI-tree bounds and tap `x`/`y`), not PNG pixels. The executor converts them with the frame's [`acos_protocol::FrameMeta::display_origin`]; a region the frame does not cover (the status bar or navigation band above/below the ART app-area capture) fails loudly instead of cropping a shifted region.

At least one criterion must be present; `text_ocr` is recognised but has no implementation in this build (the executor returns `UNSUPPORTED_ASSERTION`, never a pass). `hash` is the lowercase/uppercase hex SHA-256 of the cropped region's tightly packed RGBA8 bytes (row-major). `equals_png` names a PNG relative to the scenario file; it must be the same size as the region, or the same size as the frame (in which case the same region is cropped from it).

equals_png.description: Exact RGBA reference image for the region.

hash.description: Expected SHA-256 of the region's RGBA8 bytes.

max_distinct_colors.description: Maximum number of distinct RGBA colours in the region.

min_distinct_colors.description: Minimum number of distinct RGBA colours in the region.

text_ocr.description: Text expected to appear in the region (OCR is not implemented today).

x.description: Region left edge in display pixels.

y.description: Region top edge in display pixels.

RegionMask.description:
A rectangle excluded from screenshot comparison (clock, status bar, ...).

Bounds are **display pixels**, like every other rectangle in the scenario format; the executor maps them onto the frame with the frame's `display_origin`.

reason.description: Why this region is nondeterministic (documented, not decorative).

oneOf.description: Recreate the task only; app data is shared.

settle_timeout_ms.description: P12b: strict/fast settle deadline for the relaunched tree (milliseconds).

ResourceBudget.description:
Hard resource budgets for one request or one scenario.

Every field is opt-in; `None` means "use the engine default". The engine must return `RESOURCE_LIMIT`/`TIMEOUT` when a budget is exhausted instead of silently exceeding it.

memory_mib.description: Maximum resident memory attributable to this request/session, in MiB.

baseline.description: Baseline PNG path, relative to the scenario file or workspace root.

tolerance.description: Maximum allowed fraction of changed pixels in `0.0..=1.0`.

Selector.description: A node selector. See the module docs for the stable matching rules.

hint.description: Hint matcher (`TextView.getHint()`, e.g. an EditText placeholder).

id.description: Android resource id (`pkg:id/name`), or a bare local id (`name`).

include_invisible.description:
Also match nodes that are not visible to the user.

Default `false`: a selector matches only nodes the user can see (`UiNode::visible`, which follows `View.isVisibleToUser()`: shown, and its clipped visible rect non-empty). A warm-mounted page parked off screen is present in the tree but is not a selector match, so `wait_for`/`assert_text`/`assert_visible`/`tap` can never silently act on invisible content. Set it to `true` only for a deliberate check of an off-screen/invisible node (`assert_not_visible`, `assert_state {visible: false}`, diagnostics).

index.description: Zero-based occurrence among otherwise matching nodes.

Step.description:
A scenario step.

On the wire a step is a one-key map: `- launch: {activity: .MainActivity}`. The struct has one optional field per step kind; validation enforces that **exactly one** is present. (A Rust enum would map to YAML `!tag` syntax with `serde_yaml_ng`, which is not the agent-facing format.)

assert_region.description:
Assert a rectangular region of a fresh host-observed frame.

The region is in **display pixels** (tree bounds, tap points and this region share one space); the executor converts it to frame pixels with the frame's `display_origin`.

assert_screenshot.description: Assert a screenshot against a baseline.

assert_windows.description: Assert the window stack order (bottom to top) and focus.

call_activity_method.description: Invoke an explicitly injected test hook. Optional and only safe for debuggable/source-owned builds; never for arbitrary third-party APKs.

capture.description: Capture a frame into the artifacts directory.

StepSettle.description: The settle rule an input step asks for. `strict` is the default and evidence for every assertion; `fast` is the navigation rule for a screen that never settles (a JS auto-advance timer, an endless animation) and never backs a pass; `content` (SE2, ADR-0026 decision 3) is the content-stable rule for a screen that animates forever in pixels: it is settled when the UI tree content signature is unchanged for a bounded window. Content settle backs UI/text assertions only; a pixel/frame assertion bound to it fails closed.

oneOf.description: Content-stable settle: the UI tree content signature is unchanged for the bounded window even if pixels keep animating (SE2). Backs UI/text assertions; never a pixel/frame assertion.

expect_change.description:
SE1: fail the step when the settled frame's pixels are unchanged.

Opt-in and strict-only: `expect_change: true` with `settle: fast` is rejected at scenario-validation time, because a fast frame may be mid-animation and can never back a claim.

settle.description: Settle rule for this input (`strict` default, `fast` navigation).

settle_timeout_ms.description: P12b: strict/fast settle deadline for this tap (milliseconds).

TextAssertion.description: Assert a node's text (and optionally its exact bounds).

timeout_ms.description: Event-driven timeout; the runtime waits for a matching frame/tree, never for a fixed sleep.

TextMatch.description:
A text matching rule: exactly one of `exact`, `contains`, `regex`.

A struct rather than an enum so the agent-facing YAML/JSON form is a plain map (`text: {exact: "Greet"}`) and not a YAML `!tag`.

exact.description: Full string equality (no trimming or normalisation).

expect_change.description: SE1: fail the step when the settled frame's pixels are unchanged.

settle.description: Settle rule for this input (`strict` default, `fast` navigation).

settle_timeout_ms.description: P12b: strict/fast settle deadline for this type action (milliseconds).

require_visible.description: Require the matched node to be visible.

WindowOrderAssertion.description:
`assert_windows`: the window stack in policy z order, bottom first.

This is the LAYER1 assertion: it reads the tree's `windows[]` block (the host's AOSP layer policy, not insertion order), so an application overlay that is drawn and tapped above an activity can only pass when the reported stack actually says so.

focus.description: Optional expected kind of the focused window.

focus_type.description: Optional expected `LayoutParams.TYPE_*` name of the focused window. This is the precise form: the activity is `TYPE_BASE_APPLICATION`, a dialog is `TYPE_APPLICATION`, and both have kind `application`.

order.description: Expected window kinds, bottom to top (`application`, `application_overlay`, `sub_window`, …). The count must match exactly: a missing or extra window is a failure, never silently ignored.

types.description: Optional expected `LayoutParams.TYPE_*` names, bottom to top. When present this must have the same length as `order`.

animations.description:
P12: per-session framework animation scales (`on`/`off`, default `on`).

`off` sets Android's three animation scales to 0 for functional checks; it is never for animation/transition testing. Launch-time only.

api_level.description: Android API level required, when the scenario pins one.

expect_error.description:
SE2b: the exact failure a **negative** scenario must produce.

`expectation: fail` only says "the run did not pass"; it accepts ANY failing step, so a negative control can go red (or green) for the wrong reason and still look like proof. `expect_error` pins the error code and, optionally, the `details.reason` of the failure. A run that fails with another code/reason is a harness error, never a successful negative.

insets.description:
W7b: per-session app-window inset model (`carve`/`report`).

Selects the model for this scenario exactly as `ACOS_WM_INSETS` does, and takes precedence over the environment. A scenario that pins the model is self-contained: it cannot silently change meaning when the build default or the caller's environment changes. Launch-time only; the Rust VM has no window insets and ignores it.

name.description: Human/agent-readable name (also used in the verdict).
